messages:
Ana (People Ops): Quick share — built a 15min manager prep + async calibration snippet deck for the upcoming performance cycle. Short, bite-sized prompts for self-review reading, 1:1 agenda, and a simple rubric. Posting sample below. Use freely and tweak. :sparkles:

Jamal (Engineering Manager): Awesome, will use for next week. can you make the rubric a 3-tier so ICs don't get confused?

Ana (People Ops): Yep — kept it 3-tier intentionally (Exceeds / Meets / Needs Growth). Super short descriptors so managers can score quickly. Example in the snippet.

Lisa (Eng): fwiw could we add a one-sentence coaching tip per tier? helps new managers.

Ana (People Ops): good call — added one-liners. also added a tiny checklist for 1:1s (what to ask, evidence to collect).

Sanjay (People Ops Lead): If we plan a calibration meeting, can we include a 10-min pre-read template for managers to paste in? saves time.

Ana (People Ops): done. pasted everything below — copy/paste friendly. happy to make a Google Slide if folks want visuals.

hr-bot: Reminder: performance cycle kickoff doc is at https://redwood.internal/perf/kickoff — cycle opens in 5 days.

Ana (People Ops): [SNIPPET — Manager 15min prep + Async calibration pack]

````
1) Quick manager prep (15 minutes)
- Read the employee's self-review highlights (3 bullets) — 2 min
- Review last cycle goals + 1 recent deliverable/examples — 5 min
- Rate on rubric (Exceeds / Meets / Needs Growth) with 1-sentence rationale — 3 min
- Draft 1:1 agenda with at least one coaching question and one action item — 5 min

2) Suggested 1:1 agenda (30 min)
- 5m: Quick check-in (how are you) and one win
- 10m: Discuss self-review highlights + clarify examples
- 10m: Development / career conversation (ask: what would you pursue next?)
- 5m: Agree next steps + owner/timeline

3) Self-review highlights prompt (send to ICs)
- Please paste 3 short bullets: 1) top contribution this cycle, 2) biggest learning, 3) one ask from your manager. Keep each bullet <= 140 chars.

4) Simple 3-tier rubric (copyable)
- Exceeds: Consistently delivered beyond expectations; examples show impact and ownership. Coaching tip: call out specific behaviors to replicate.
- Meets: Delivered expected outcomes reliably; examples cover quality and timeliness. Coaching tip: acknowledge and set stretch in one area.
- Needs Growth: Outcomes not consistently met; examples show gaps. Coaching tip: focus on one concrete skill and next-step with timeline.

5) One-sentence rationale template (for managers)
- "Rating: [Tier]. Evidence: [one concrete example]. Next step: [one action + owner + timeline]."

6) Async calibration pre-read (copy for each manager)
- Employee: [Name]
- Role/Level: [Role / Level]
- Manager provisional rating: [Tier]
- 1-paragraph summary (3-4 lines) of evidence and risk areas
- Anything to surface in calibration: [e.g., competing projects, ambiguous success metrics]

7) Quick examples (paste into convo)
- Self-review highlight: "Led cross-team rollout of caching layer; reduced p95 from 450ms -> 220ms; mentored 2 junior devs."
- Manager rationale: "Meets. Delivered the feature with measurable latency wins; needs clearer handoff docs for scale."

````

Jamal (Engineering Manager): This is fantastic. I might shorten the 1-paragraph summary to 2-3 sentences for time-boxing during calibration.

Ana (People Ops): yep — feel free to truncate. our goal is to make calibration <10m per person in the meeting.

Lisa (Eng): can the self-review bullets be enforced by the form? we still get essays sometimes.

Ana (People Ops): we can tweak the Google Form to limit characters. will do.

Sanjay (People Ops Lead): thanks Ana — can you drop this into the perf kickoff doc and link in the weekly roundup? i'll add to the manager playbook.

Ana (People Ops): on it. cc @Jamal if you want me to adapt the wording for eng-specific examples. :thumbsup:
